researcher_notes: Iran FLNG = the Exmar 'Caribbean FLNG' / Hemla project. Strong lead but no url_verifier PASS secured before wrap-up, so left UNRESOLVED rather than cite unverified. Documented milestone: NIOC signed a contract in October 2017 with IFLNG (a JV of Norway's Hemla and Iran's Kharg Gas Refining Co.) to deploy Belgium/Exmar's 0.5 mtpa 'Caribbean FLNG' at Pars Service Port (gas from South Pars refinery Phase 7), targeting first LNG end-2018; the Majlis energy committee put the deal on hold in December 2017 and it was never built (cancelled). Candidate independent sources to verify on a follow-up: azernews.az ('Iran signs first FLNG contract with Norway', 2017), parstoday.ir, offshore-energy.biz, neftegazru.com. Project never reached a formal FID; the closest investment milestone is the Oct-2017 charter/build contract (2017). FID year not staged because no source was run through url_verifier.

Iran LNG (NIOC) at Tombak/Bandar Tombak, South Pars Phase 12; T1 is one of the two original 5.4 mtpa main trains. CAVEAT: a formal FID for the two large trains was never publicly taken (substatus 'planned' = FID still outstanding); the original project launch was ~2006-2007 with no Western-style FID announcement. Year 2023 reflects the verified March-2023 official revival/relaunch of the project (work restarted, trains 1-2 targeted for ~2025 start-up) — the most recent and best-documented investment-planning milestone covering the main trains. Milestone-to-year mapping is uncertain (could alternatively reference the ~2006-07 launch), hence tier 'low'. Year 2023 confirmed on three independent outlets (Enerdata 13 Mar 2023; Natural Gas Intelligence; Iran International), all PASS url_verifier on '2023'+'Iran LNG'.

Iran LNG (NIOC), Tombak, South Pars Phase 12; T2 is the second of the two original 5.4 mtpa main trains. Same basis and caveat as T1 (st_id 1777): no formal FID was ever taken for the large trains (substatus 'planned'); year 2023 reflects the verified March-2023 project revival/relaunch (the most recent investment-planning milestone), with milestone-to-year mapping uncertain (tier 'low'). Confirmed on three independent outlets (Enerdata, Natural Gas Intelligence, Iran International), all PASS url_verifier on '2023'+'Iran LNG'.

Iran LNG (NIOC), Tombak, South Pars Phase 12; T3 is the 1.5 mtpa mid-scale train. Substatus 'actual' fits: T3 is the concrete piece that the March-2023 revival actually advanced — Iran restarted work and put the 1.5 mtpa mid-scale train into construction (reported ~50% complete by Sep 2023, commissioning targeted ~2026). Year 2023 = the de-facto investment go-ahead/revival decision (no formal Western-style 'FID' press release exists; the restart is the functional investment decision). Confirmed on three independent outlets all dated/anchored to 2023 (Enerdata 13 Mar 2023 'restarted work on the 10.8 Mt/year Iran LNG'; Natural Gas Intelligence; Iran International), all PASS url_verifier on '2023'+'Iran LNG'.

Kangan LNG = a private-sector mid-scale project (2 mtpa, two trains) on a 25 ha site at the Port of Tombak near Kangan, Bushehr; planned start-up was ~2023. No FID year is documented and no verifiable source could be staged: the project's own website (kanganlng.com) no longer resolves (DNS ENOTFOUND / 404), and no independent outlet reports an FID or investment-decision year. Project appears dormant. UNRESOLVED — no FID year establishable within constraints.

North Pars LNG = NIOC/Pars Oil & Gas Co. + China's CNOOC, a planned four-train, ~20 mtpa LNG plant at Tombak fed by the North Pars field. This project never reached a formal FID. Year 2006 = the China-Iran North Pars development agreement (CNOOC-NIOC MoU signed Sep 2006, extended Dec 2006 to include the 4-train LNG facility) — the strongest binding investment-agreement milestone that actually occurred — confirmed on two independent outlets (OilPrice; Oil & Gas Journal), both PASS url_verifier on '2006'+'North Pars'. CAVEAT: the formal development/EPC contract (the true FID/investment commitment) was targeted to be signed by 31 Aug 2007 (Egypt Oil & Gas, dated 2007, PASS url_verifier on '2007'+'North Pars') but was never finalized; project suspended ~2011-12 under sanctions. If GEM's 'proposed' entry already carries 2006, a reviewer may prefer 2007 (the planned-contract/FID-target year) for this FID milestone.

Persian LNG = NIOC + Shell + Repsol, South Pars Phases 13-14. A formal FID was never taken. Documented planning: Shell/Repsol joined ~2004 (HoA), with an original aim to finalize contracts/FID by ~2006 and start up ~2012-14; the FID slipped repeatedly through 2008-2009 and Iran ended the talks in 2010, awarding the upstream to a domestic consortium. No open-access source could be run through url_verifier that ties a single FID year to 'Persian LNG' (the strongest statements — original FID target 2006 — sit on paywalled S&P Global/IHS Markit and Lloyd's List pages that soft-error). UNRESOLVED: planned-FID year (~2006 original target) not verifiable within constraints.

Qeshm LNG = a ~$250M, three-train (3 x 1.15 mtpa) project promoted by the Qeshm Free Zone, announced ~June 2017; no development updates since 2017 and presumed cancelled. The project never reached a formal FID; the only datable milestone is the 2017 announcement (a proposal, not an investment decision). No source could be run through url_verifier before wrap-up to stage a specific FID year. UNRESOLVED — no FID year establishable (project never advanced past 2017 announcement).

Best identification: this GEM record most likely corresponds to the Pars LNG JV (NIOC 50% / Total 30% / Petronas 20%), South Pars Phase 11, a two-train ~10 mtpa plant near Tombak; the shareholders' agreement was signed in 2007 and Total/Petronas withdrew ~2008, so no FID was taken. A candidate source (gulfoilandgas.com mainnews id=419) intermittently PASSED url_verifier on '2007'+'Pars LNG' but returned INCONSISTENT content across repeat fetches (a second call failed to find the same tokens), indicating an unstable/dynamic page — so it is NOT citeable. The identity of GEM's 'South Pars LNG Terminal' record vs the Pars LNG project is also not independently confirmed (gem.wiki was unreadable here). UNRESOLVED: no stable, verifiable source ties a single FID year to this record.
